issues.legal_issue: A court may not issue mandatory interlocutory directions to re-tender property while an unchallenged subsisting lease governs occupation, without first deciding the lessee’s legal entitlement to remain.
material_facts: A public-interest writ sought, among other things, leasing the property at market rent, but did not seek to quash the existing lease.
The lease remained in force, and the lessee was not alleged to be in unauthorised occupation.

At the interlocutory stage, the High Court directed the municipal corporation to invite offers and later directed it to lease the property to the highest bidder and require the existing lessee to vacate.
issues.conclusion: The interlocutory directions were beyond the relief claimed and were passed without deciding the validity or effect of the subsisting lease; they were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: An interim mandatory order must be supported by just and tangible reasons and must remain within the scope of the relief sought. A court cannot direct re-letting before determining the effect of an unchallenged subsisting contract or whether the existing occupant is legally entitled to remain.

rule.if: public_interest_writ_proceeding and subsisting_lease_contract and not lease_validity_challenged and mandatory_interlocutory_reletting_order and occupancy_rights_not_adjudicated

predicates.public_interest_writ_proceeding: A person brings a public-interest writ proceeding concerning the management or leasing of public property.
predicates.subsisting_lease_contract: The public body and the occupant are bound by a lease that remains in force.
predicates.lease_validity_challenged: The proceeding challenges the validity of the lease governing the occupant’s possession.
predicates.mandatory_interlocutory_reletting_order: The court orders the public body, before final determination, to invite offers or re-let the property.
predicates.occupancy_rights_not_adjudicated: The court issues the re-letting direction without first deciding whether the existing occupant is legally entitled to remain.

issues.definition: When a public-interest writ concerns property governed by an unchallenged subsisting lease, a mandatory interlocutory re-letting direction made without deciding the occupant’s legal entitlement is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: A court-directed grant of a municipal lease must follow the statutory procedure for recommending the proposal and obtaining prior government sanction.
material_facts: The High Court directed the municipal corporation to invite offers and subsequently to lease the premises to the highest bidder.
The Supreme Court held that those directions disregarded the statutory procedure governing the grant of a lease by the municipal corporation.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s directions were set aside for disregarding the mandatory lease-grant procedure.
issues.legal_principle: Section 157 of the Himachal Pradesh Municipal Corporation Act, 1994 requires a proposal for a lease to be recommended by the municipal corporation and requires prior government sanction before the corporation executes the agreement.

predicates.municipal_lease_grant_proceeding: A proceeding concerns the grant of a lease by a municipal corporation.
predicates.court_directs_lease_grant_without_requir: The court directs a lease to be granted without the municipal proposal being recommended and prior government sanction being obtained.

issues.definition: A court direction to grant a municipal lease is invalid when it bypasses the required recommendation and prior government sanction.

issues.legal_issue: Outstanding dues owed by a state corporation to a municipal corporation may be addressed through state intervention and, if unresolved, statutory recovery measures.
material_facts: The writ sought recovery of outstanding municipal dues, with particular emphasis on amounts said to be owed by the state corporation in respect of the premises.
The State was a party to the proceedings, and the Court stated that it should seek a suitable lawful solution.

The Court observed that if the corporation could not meet the claim, the State might provide financial assistance; otherwise the municipal corporation could use statutory recovery remedies, including eviction after termination of the contract.
issues.conclusion: The State was required to take the initiative to find a lawful solution expeditiously; if the dues remained unresolved, the municipal corporation could pursue statutory recovery and, following termination of the contract, eviction.
issues.legal_principle: Outstanding public dues may be addressed through state intervention, including financial assistance where necessary; failing resolution, the creditor public body may resort to statutory recovery remedies. Eviction of a contractual occupant may follow termination of the contract.

predicates.public_dues_recovery_proceeding: A proceeding seeks recovery of public dues owed to a municipal body.
predicates.state_corporation_owes_municipal_dues: A corporation owned by the State owes dues to the municipal body.
predicates.dues_remain_unresolved: The parties have not resolved the claim for outstanding dues.

issues.definition: When a state corporation owes unresolved dues to a municipal body, the State must seek a lawful resolution and the municipality may pursue statutory recovery.

issues.legal_issue: A participant in a court-directed tender conducted subject to pending litigation acquires no right to the property but is entitled to repayment of the earnest money deposited.
material_facts: A tender process was conducted pursuant to interim court directions and was expressly subject to the outcome of the pending legal proceedings.
A tender participant deposited earnest money for participating in the process.
The Supreme Court held that participation created no right to the premises, but entitled the participant to return of the deposit with interest.
issues.conclusion: The earnest money was ordered to be refunded with interest, with a higher interest consequence if repayment was not made within the directed time.
issues.legal_principle: Where participation in a tender is expressly subject to the outcome of pending proceedings, it creates no right to the property; the participant is entitled to repayment of the earnest money with interest.

predicates.court_directed_tender_during_pending_lit: A tender is conducted under court directions while legal proceedings concerning the property remain pending.
predicates.tender_subject_to_litigation_outcome: The tender process is expressly made subject to the outcome of the pending proceedings.
predicates.earnest_money_deposited: A participant pays earnest money to take part in the tender.

issues.definition: A participant who deposits earnest money in a court-directed tender expressly subject to pending litigation is entitled to a refund with interest, but acquires no right to the property.
